doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Playing, records and the Hyman album
title: Desert island recording, Basie Live in Japan
summary: Asked about a desert island pick, Butch cites Basie's 1978 Live in Japan, with over a hundred albums behind him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. I don’t know if you’ve been asked the typical “if you could pick ten recordings because you’re stuck on a desert island” question — but, if I was to ask that, I mean you don’t have to go through it but would there be any recordings included that you play on?
Because I have a candidate by the way.
I would have to say that if I did include one of mine, which, now that you bring it up, offhand I wouldn’t, but if I did out of all the albums, I’ve done over a hundred, a hundred

and some albums with everybody. I mean I recorded with Basie, recorded with Mulligan, recorded with Alberta Hunter. Here’s a name for you, Dolly Dawn, there’s one, remember that one. And a lot of different people. There’d be a Basie recording which is called “Live in Japan.” And we recorded that one, not the last one that was recorded about 2007 I think or 2006, but way before when it was recorded back in 1978. The band was smoking hot and I just had all of my you-know-what together. And we were a unit. It was glorious and it was beautiful, and that would be the one. Other than that it’s a lot of stuff that sometimes I can listen to but barely.
